cases.headline: DUK has climbed back from a morning dip; buy only if it breaks above the morning high, with a tight exit if it slips back.
cases.bull:
The bull case is modest. DUK gapped down 0.93% (open 129.38 vs prev close 130.59), then reclaimed most of it: last 129.98, above VWAP 129.83, and the opening range (129.19-130.075) was a strong 0.88-point rejection of the low. Relative volume is 2.63x, though the first bar is 453k and the next two are only 47k and 55k, so the volume is front-loaded. Higher closes (129.81, 129.85, 129.98) show steady buying. The stock sits 0.07% under OR high, and it is well above the 20-day average (126.75). The index is flat (-0.07%), so no headwind.

Entry: a 5-minute close above 130.14, the scanner trigger, which is just above OR high. Stop: the plan's 129.19 is 0.95 away, about 1.8 ATRs, too wide for a $1,000 account. At $5 risk that is roughly 5 shares, only about $650 notional. I would tighten the stop to just under VWAP/range midpoint (~129.60), risking about 0.54. Target: 132.04 is 1.9 away, which is ambitious for a utility. Realistic is prior-day gap fill zone 130.59, then 131.0, for about 1R.

Wrong if: price loses VWAP (129.83) on a closing basis, or breakout volume stays near 50k per bar.
cases.bear:
Rebuttals. The "steady buying" is thin: closes of 129.81, 129.85 and 129.98 are gains of 0.04 and 0.13 on only 47k and 55k shares, against 453k in the first bar. That is drift, not conviction. The 2.63x relvol is almost entirely the opening print, so it says little about a breakout. Price is only 0.15 above VWAP (129.83), well within one ATR (0.525), so "reclaimed" overstates it. The gap-fill target at 130.59 and prior-day low 129.96 matter: price sits right on 129.96, which is overhead and underfoot noise. Prior high 131.42 caps the 132.04 target. The Bull's 129.60 stop is inside the opening range, 0.38 above the range low, so it is easy to hit in chop. The 20-day average (126.75) is irrelevant intraday.

Bear case: honest but weak. The stock is below yesterday's close (130.59), and a failed push at 130.075 would leave a lower high. Only three bars exist, so there is no evidence of a failed breakout yet.

Short trigger: a 5-minute close below 129.80 (under VWAP and the 129.81 bar low area). Stop 130.15. Target 129.25 (range low), about 1.5R. Edge is marginal; staying out is the preferred call unless a clean break occurs.

**Verdict: stay out / no trade for now.**

judge.title: DUK gap-down reclaim: small long on an opening-range break
judge.text: DUK opened 0.93% lower at 129.38, but it has recovered to 129.98. That is above VWAP at 129.83 and only 0.07% under the opening-range high of 130.075, on 2.63x relative volume with a flat index (-0.07%). The Bear is right that the volume is front-loaded: 453k shares in the first bar against 47k and 55k since. The 132.04 rule target also sits above yesterday's high of 131.42, so I aim for 130.95 instead, which is past the gap-fill level of 130.59 and below that ceiling. I use the Bull's tighter stop of 129.60, under VWAP: the risk is 0.54 (about one 5-minute ATR of 0.525) against a 0.81 reward, which is 1.5R. Conviction stays at 2 because only three bars exist, the 129.60 stop can be hit by chop inside the range, and my one similar past call (n=1, rule plan +0.71R) proves nothing.

cases.headline: JPM is pressing the top of its first-15-minute range; buy only if it breaks above 334.92 and aim for a partial refill of this morning's gap.
cases.bull:
Bull case, kept honest: JPM is holding the top of its opening range. Last is 334.10 against an OR of 332.32-334.75, about 0.19% below the high, and above VWAP of 333.35. The open bar was heavy (691k) and the next two bars were light and stable, with higher lows (332.32, then 333.51). Relative volume of 1.98 shows real interest. The index is flat (-0.07%), so there is no headwind.

Entry: only on a break of 334.92, just above the OR high, ideally on a 5-minute close with volume above the last two bars (153k, 109k). Don't chase early.

Stop: the plan's 332.32 is 2.60 away, about 1.5 ATR, which is wide. At $5 risk that means roughly 1-2 shares, so costs bite. A tighter stop under VWAP (~333.30) is about 1.6 away, but it is easily noise.

Target: the plan's 340.11 is +5.19, about 2:1, but it is ambitious. It means reclaiming yesterday's gap-down area and the 20-day average of 339.28. Realistically, take 337-338 or partial profits near 336.

Wrong if: price closes back below VWAP 333.35, or fails at 334.75 and retests 332.32. Also, the stock gapped down 1.4% and sits below the 20DMA, so the trend is against us. The edge is thin.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: Relative volume of 1.98 is almost entirely the 691k open bar. The next two bars fell to 153k and 109k, so volume is fading, not confirming. Calling the higher lows "real interest" is generous: three bars is too little to establish a trend. Price at 334.10 sits only 0.75 above VWAP of 333.35, which is less than half an ATR (1.69), so "above VWAP" is nearly meaningless. The flat index (-0.07%) offers no tailwind either. The Bull concedes the real problems: a 1.4% gap down from 338.21, a close below the 20DMA of 339.28, and a 2.60 stop that allows only 1-2 shares, so costs eat the edge. The 340.11 target runs into yesterday's range (336.67-346.52) and the 20DMA, which is overhead supply.

Case for staying out: the breakout trigger of 334.92 is only 0.82 above last, with three bars of data, and the first thrust to 334.75 already got rejected.

Short idea, low conviction: a 5-minute close back below 333.35 (VWAP) after a failed push at 334.75. Stop 334.95. Target 332.32, the OR low, about 1.0 reward against 1.6 risk, which is under 1:1. That is not tradable.

Verdict: stay out, no edge either way.

judge.title: JPM: small long on opening-range break, tighter stop under VWAP, target just below yesterday's close
judge.text: The Bull's structure holds. Last trade is 334.10, just 0.19% below the opening-range high of 334.75 and above VWAP at 333.35, with higher lows (332.32, then 333.51), relative volume of 1.98 and a flat index (-0.07%), so a break of 334.92 has a clear path. The Bear is right about two things: volume faded from 691k to 109k, and the rule plan's 332.32 stop (2.60 away) and 340.11 target ask too much of a stock that gapped down 1.4% below its 20DMA of 339.28. I therefore resize the trade: the stop goes to 333.30, under VWAP and the 333.51 bar low (1.62 risk), and the target to 338.10, just below the 338.21 prior close where gap-fill sellers wait (3.18 reward, about 2:1). Conviction stays at 2 because the down gap and fading volume make a failed breakout quite possible, and my one past call (n=1) is no evidence either way.

cases.headline: EMR is pushing at its morning high, but the push was rejected on heavy volume, so we stay out for now.
cases.bull:
The honest long case is modest. EMR opened 160.76, ran to 162.18 in the first 15 minutes, and holds at 161.72, just above VWAP 161.68, with relvol 1.52 and the third bar's 147k volume showing real buying interest into the high. It sits 0.28% under the OR high of 162.18 while the index is flat (-0.07%), so the strength is stock-specific.

Entry: only on a 5-minute close above 162.26, the plan's trigger, which confirms the OR break. Don't buy ahead of it.

Stop: the plan's 160.53 is 1.73 away, so $5 risk buys about 2 shares, which is clumsy and makes costs relatively heavy. A tighter stop just under VWAP/OR midpoint, around 161.20 (~1.06 risk, ~4 shares), is more practical, though it is closer to noise at atr5 0.71.

Target: the plan's 165.72 is unrealistic intraday, since it sits at prior-day-high territory (165.10) and 2x the OR range. A realistic target is ~163.70, about 1.5R on the tighter stop, near 2x OR range extension.

Wrong if: price closes back below VWAP (~161.68) after the break, or volume fades on the push. Also, 20-day MA 165.13 overhead is a headwind. This is a marginal setup.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: The Bull calls 147k volume "real buying," but that bar opened 161.74, hit 162.18 and closed 161.72, so it rejected the high and gave back the whole move. That is heavy volume with no net progress, which looks more like absorption at the OR high than accumulation. "Just above VWAP" is 0.04, under a tenth of atr5 (0.71), so it is effectively on VWAP and shows no strength. The index is flat, so "stock-specific" strength is just a 0.6% move on three bars. The Bull's 161.20 stop is about 0.5 below VWAP, inside one atr5 of noise, and the 1.5R target of 163.70 sits against the overhead 165.10 gap-fill zone and the 165.13 20-day MA. The Bull concedes all of this is marginal. I agree, and at a tenth of risk in costs, marginal loses.

Bear case: the upper-wick rejection at 162.18 could become a failed breakout, but there are only three bars and no confirmed lower high. Yesterday's low of 160.17 and the OR low of 160.53 are close support, so a short has limited room.

Verdict: stay out. A short only triggers on a 5-minute close below 161.30 (under the 161.44 bar low), stop 162.25, target 160.55. That is about 0.95 risk for 0.75 reward, which is negative, so no trade.

judge.title: No trade: EMR: opening-range break not yet earned, pass
judge.text: The deciding fact is the 09:40 bar. It traded 147k shares, more than the first two bars combined (about 51k), and touched 162.18. It then closed at 161.72, giving back the whole move, which looks like sellers absorbing buying at the high rather than a clean breakout. The price sits only 0.04 above VWAP (161.68), and the index is flat at -0.07%. Relative volume of 1.52 is decent but not exceptional. The stock also trades below yesterday's high of 165.10 and its 20-day average of 165.13, after closing near yesterday's low at 160.65. The plan's 1.73-point stop is more than twice atr5 (0.71), while a tighter 161.20 stop sits inside noise, so with costs near 0.1R the edge looks marginal. My one prior similar case (n=1, where I passed and the rule trade made +0.71R) is too thin to override today's evidence. If forced, I would go long on a break of 162.26 with a stop at 161.20 and a target at 163.85, which is 1.5R.

cases.headline: FDX bounced back to where it opened but has not proved it can break higher, so we stay out.
cases.bull:
**Bull case, honestly sized.** FDX opened 325.00, flushed to 323.00 in the first bar, and recovered to 325.02 by 09:45. That is a V-shaped reclaim of the opening range (323.00 to 325.13) on relvol 1.62, while the index is down 0.23%, so relative strength is real. Price sits above VWAP (324.09), and the stock is far above its 20-day average (311.09) and above yesterday's high (324.43).

**Entry:** a 5-minute close above 325.66 (day high), not the scanner's 325.29, which is only 0.27 above last and sits inside the noise (atr5 1.47). Waiting costs some edge but filters fakeouts.

**Stop:** the scanner's 323.00 is about 2.3 away, roughly 1.6 ATR. At a $5 risk that is only ~2 shares, so costs eat a meaningful chunk. A tighter stop below VWAP (~323.9) gives a ~1.8 risk and ~2.8 shares, but it gets whipsawed more easily.

**Target:** 329.88 is ~4.6 above the trigger, about 3 ATR with only 4 bars of evidence. A realistic target is ~328 (about 2R from a VWAP stop).

**Wrong if:** price loses VWAP, or the 323.00 low retests, or relvol fades. Edge is modest, and the setup is unproven.
cases.bear:
Rebuttal: The "relative strength" claim is thin. The index is down only 0.23%, and FDX's move today is 0.0 (open 325.00, last 325.02). It has gone nowhere, so it is not outperforming. The V-reclaim is also not clean: volume fell from 41,820 in the first bar to 26-32k since, so the reclaim came on fading participation. Being far above the 20-day (311.09) is extension, not support. Yesterday's high of 324.43 is only 0.6 below last, so it is not a meaningful cushion. Relvol 1.62 is only mild. The Bull's own 325.66 trigger is just 0.64 above last, within half an ATR (1.47), so it's a coin flip. Also the 4-bar sample is too small to support a 329.88 target.

Bear case: 325.66 was the 09:45 high and the bar closed at 325.02, well off it, a rejection wick. Price is only 0.93 above VWAP, so there's no real extension, and a short has little edge either.

Verdict: stay out. For a logged short only: trigger below 324.00 (under VWAP 324.09), stop 325.70, target 323.00. That is about 1.7 risk for 1.0 reward, so it is unattractive. Pass.

judge.title: No trade: FDX: V-reclaim of the opening range, but a rejection at 325.66 and fading volume mean pass
judge.text: The Bull's best point holds: FDX flushed to 323.00 and recovered to 325.02, above VWAP (324.09) and yesterday's high (324.43). But the Bear is right that it is flat on the day (open 325.00, last 325.02) against an index down only 0.23%, so the relative strength is thin. The 09:45 bar pushed to 325.66 and closed back at 325.02, a rejection wick. Volume also faded from 41,820 to 26-32k per bar during the reclaim, and relvol of 1.62 is only mild. A credible long needs a break above 325.66 with a stop under VWAP near 323.90, which is about 1.8 of risk, more than an ATR of 1.47. That buys only about 2-3 shares on a $5 risk, and reaching a 2R target near 328.60 would mean going well past anything four bars have shown, so the edge looks too marginal to survive costs.

cases.name: Southern Co
cases.headline: rel. volume 5.6x, +2.0% today
cases.bull: Up 2% on a day SPY is down 1.1%. Opening volume 5.6x normal. Steady climb all morning, now above VWAP (93.70) and above yesterday's high (94.19), so it is breaking out of yesterday's range.
cases.bear: This looks like a defensive rotation into utilities on a risk-off day, not news about SO. It is already 1.9% above the opening range and 0.6% above VWAP. Volume has faded since 10:45. The mechanical stop (94.10) is only 0.25% away and sits inside the midday noise.

judge.title: LONG on a new day high
judge.text: The relative strength is real, but buying the middle of the range invites a stop-out on noise. Trigger 94.52 (above the 94.495 day high), stop 94.05 (below the 11:00 low of 94.06), target 95.22 (1.5R), conviction 3. Leverage 1x.

cases.name: Charles Schwab
cases.headline: rel. volume 1.8x, +1.1% today
cases.bull: Gapped down 0.7%, made its low in the first 5 minutes (89.76), then reversed above the open, VWAP and yesterday's close. A clean intraday reversal.
cases.bear: It is back inside yesterday's range (91.54–93.79), so there are sellers overhead up to 93.79. Broker stocks are high-beta on a falling market. It has stalled under 92.20 for an hour with lighter volume.

judge.text: A stalled high-beta name in a weak market, with overhead supply. The reversal has already been paid for.
